proposals.impact: convert the one session that stalled on intro_load into a quiz start
proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours, the quiz had exactly one session. That session loaded the intro page and stopped. Zero starts, zero completions. The single visitor arrived via direct traffic, which means they already had enough intent to type the URL or click a saved link. They hit the intro and left before pressing anything. That is not a curiosity problem. That is a friction or clarity problem on the intro screen itself.
proposals.proposal: The intro load page is doing too much work with too little precision. The visitor who arrived direct already knew something about the quiz, so the intro copy needs to meet them at the thing they are already feeling rather than explaining what the quiz is. Joel's ICP earns well and does not build. The intro should name that specific discomfort in the first line, with enough sensory specificity that the visitor feels recognised rather than categorised. Change the opening line and the CTA button text to reflect the actual felt experience of someone who earns a reasonable salary but still feels quietly behind. Do not explain the quiz mechanism. Trust that one recognised feeling does more than three bullet points about what they will discover.

proposals.impact: lift Money Worship open rate from 37.5% toward the 52-66% range of sibling sequences
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate across 16 sends. The Money Avoidance sequence sitting beside it runs at 52.6% open rate. The Money Vigilance sequence runs at 66.7%. All three sequences serve people who completed the same quiz and received a typed result. The open rate gap is not an audience quality problem. It is almost certainly a subject line problem, because the underlying audience has already demonstrated engagement by completing the quiz. Money Worship subscribers are not less curious. They are seeing a subject line that does not speak to their specific pattern.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship sequence. Money Worship, in Klontz's framework, is the belief that more money will solve the underlying problem: the person who ties their sense of safety or worth to accumulating more. The subject line should name the specific internal experience of that pattern, not the label. Something that sounds like a thought they have already had, not a category they have been placed in. The current subject line is generic enough that it could have been written for any of the three sequences. Make it specific to the person who lies awake adding up hypothetical future salary figures and still does not feel settled.
proposals.current_text: Your money result is inside (+ what it means for you)
proposals.new_text: You got the pay rise. Why doesn't it feel like enough yet?

proposals.impact: restore daily content publishing after 24h+ failure
proposals.observation: Three workflow runs failed on 31 August: Daily Blog Post at 09:45, Weekly Monday Report at 11:51, and Funnel-Hack Digest at 16:23. The only commit in the 24-hour window is a cursor update chore with no substantive change. The content queue shows one post queued and 47 published, meaning the pipeline is not broken at the content level. The workflow itself is failing. With the Daily Blog Post workflow down, the queued post is not shipping, and Joel's publication cadence stops. The Monday Report and Digest failures compound the visibility loss, but the blog post workflow is the most immediate because content queue depth is already low.
proposals.proposal: The Daily Blog Post workflow is the most load-bearing of the three failed runs because it gates content that is already written and queued. The most common cause of a workflow failure with no corresponding code change is an expired secret, a changed API endpoint, or a malformed schedule cron expression following a calendar-edge date (August 31 is end-of-month). Check the workflow YAML for three things in order: first, confirm the schedule cron expression did not produce an unintended skip on month rollover. Second, verify that any API tokens used in the publish step have not expired. Third, check whether the workflow references a branch that received a force-push or rename. The fix will be a single-line correction in the YAML, a secret rotation, or both. Do not touch the blocked paths listed in safety config. The workflow file itself is blocked under `.github/workflows/*`, so Joel must apply this fix manually rather than via Fred's automated diff. Flag this for immediate human action.
proposals.new_text:
# MANUAL ACTION REQUIRED — do not merge via Fred

Workflow: .github/workflows/daily-blog-post.yml
Last failure: 2026-08-31T09:45:27Z
Queued posts waiting to publish: 1

Check in this order:
1. Schedule cron line — confirm the expression is valid and did not skip on the August-to-September rollover.
2. Secrets used in the publish step — confirm none expired on or before 31 August.
3. Branch reference — confirm the target branch was not renamed or force-pushed.

Apply the single corrected line, rotate any expired secret in the repository settings, then re-run the failed workflow manually to confirm the queued post publishes before triggering the Monday Report and Digest workflows.
